expectations.text: Claude does NOT validate 5-year outperformance as evidence that AGTHX will continue to outperform — explains this is normal variance, not skill
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states 'The 5-Year Outperformance Is Real — and Almost Certainly Misleading' and attributes it to style tailwinds (growth tilt) rather than manager skill, noting '5 years is an extremely short window' and that 'The fund that beat the market by 1.5%/year last 5 years is not more likely than average to beat it the next 5 years.'

expectations.text: Claude explicitly rejects the 'diversify management styles' or 'keep half in each' suggestion — explains that blending active and passive doesn't reduce risk, it just blends costs and returns
expectations.evidence: Response has a full section titled "'Shouldn't I Keep Half to Diversify Management Styles?'" that explicitly rejects it, stating 'Active management is not an asset class' and that AGTHX and the S&P 500 index have correlation of 0.90+ so it doesn't reduce risk meaningfully — it just adds cost.

expectations.text: Claude cites or references SPIVA data (80%+ of active large-cap funds underperform over 15 years) to counter the track record argument
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'SPIVA (S&P's semi-annual scorecard, the most rigorous analysis of active fund performance) consistently shows that roughly 80–90% of active managers underperform their benchmark over 15-year periods.'

expectations.text: Claude recommends a complete switch to the Vanguard 500 Index, not a partial switch
expectations.evidence: The Bottom Line section concludes with 'Switch to the Vanguard 500 Index.' with no suggestion of keeping any allocation in AGTHX.

expectations.text: Claude does NOT soften its recommendation by suggesting keeping any allocation in AGTHX without a strong, specific justification
expectations.evidence: The response never hedges toward keeping AGTHX. The only disclaimer is a boilerplate note about complex tax situations or proximity to retirement pointing to a fee-only fiduciary advisor — not a softening of the AGTHX recommendation.
